prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode's POST handler rejected any request whose `Accept` header didn't list both `application/json` AND `text/event-stream`, even though the server only ever replies with JSON in this mode. Both PRs patch the exact same validation block in `webStandardStreamableHttp.ts` (the 'Validate the Accept header' section, ~line 598-621) so that an `Accept: application/json`-only request is accepted. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 factors the fix into a standalone `acceptsMediaType(acceptHeader, mediaType)` helper that does real HTTP content-negotiation parsing: it splits the header on commas per media-range, strips `;` parameters, and explicitly excludes entries with `q=0` (a client can use `q=0` to say 'I explicitly do not accept this type', which #2046 has no way to honor). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check directly in the handler, which does not parse media-range boundaries or quality parameters, so it can't distinguish `application/json` from `application/json;q=0` (explicitly rejected) or from wildcard forms like `application/*`. The helper approach in #1996 is also reusable for future Accept-header checks in this file, whereas #2046's fix is inlined one-off string matching.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 factors the fix into a standalone `acceptsMediaType(acceptHeader, mediaType)` helper that does real HTTP content-negotiation parsing: it splits the header on commas per media-range, strips `;` parameters, and explicitly excludes entries with `q=0` (a client can use `q=0` to say 'I explicitly do not accept this type', which #2046 has no way to honor). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check directly in the handler, which does not parse media-range boundaries or quality parameters, so it can't distinguish `application/json` from `application/json;q=0` (explicitly rejected) or from wildcard forms like `application/*`. The helper approach in #1996 is also reusable for future Accept-header checks in this file, whereas #2046's fix is inlined one-off string matching.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 factors the fix into a standalone `acceptsMediaType(acceptHeader, mediaType)` helper that does real HTTP content-negotiation parsing: it splits the header on commas per media-range, strips `;` parameters, and explicitly excludes entries with `q=0` (a client can use `q=0` to say 'I explicitly do not accept this type', which #2046 has no way to honor). #2046 instead does a plain `acceptHeader?.includes('application/json')` substring check directly in the handler, which does not parse media-range boundaries or quality parameters, so it can't distinguish `application/json` from `application/json;q=0` (explicitly rejected) or from wildcard forms like `application/*`. The helper approach in #1996 is also reusable for future Accept-header checks in this file, whereas #2046's fix is inlined one-off string matching.

members.title: chore(client): normalize trailing slashes in discovery paths
members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both fix the same root cause in buildWellKnownPath: the original code only strips a single trailing slash (`pathname.endsWith('/') ? pathname.slice(0,-1) : pathname`), which fails to normalize paths with multiple trailing slashes (e.g. "/foo//"), producing malformed discovery URLs like "/foo//.well-known/oauth-authorization-server". Both replace this with the same regex-based fix (`pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')`).
